column2: THEME: a lava lamp. Each numeral is a body of glowing wax inside the lamp's tapered glass, in a vivid wax/liquid colour pair per lamp. At rest the wax wobbles and bulges on the beat, small blobs bud off and rejoin. Minute turn: the old numeral necks, pinches off and rises in blobs, which drift and merge into the new numeral. Hour: the lamps heat up, a big plume rises and the colours change.

THEME: a glassblower's studio. Each numeral is a gather of molten glass worked on a blowpipe, glowing orange-white and cooling to coloured glass with flat highlights. At rest the glass is turned and pulled, glowing seams move on the beat. Minute turn: the old numeral goes back into the glory hole, slumps soft, and is pulled, pinched and swung into the new numeral. Hour: a furnace door opens and a bright gather is blown into a bubble.

THEME: octopuses in a reef. Each numeral is an octopus arm curled into the digit's shape, suckers along the inside, its skin flashing chromatophore colour waves. At rest the arms curl and breathe, colour waves pulse down them on the beat. Minute turn: the arm uncoils and recurls, suckers rolling, into the new digit. Hour: an ink cloud and a full-body colour flash.

THEME: a children's pop-up book. Each numeral is a paper pop-up standing on an open spread, with tabs, slots and printed flat illustration. At rest pull-tabs slide and flaps wiggle on the beat. Minute turn: the page turns, the old pop-up folds flat into the gutter as the new spread opens and its numeral rises. Hour: a big centrepiece pop-up unfolds.

THEME: dachshunds in a park. Each numeral is a long sausage dog bending its body into the digit's shape, each with its own coat. At rest tails wag, ears flap and they sniff on the beat. Minute turn: the old dog trots out of its shape and the new dog trots in and curls into its digit. Hour: a ball is thrown and they all chase it, then return to their places.

THEME: a wooden toddler bead maze (roller-coaster wire toy). Each numeral is a bent coloured wire threaded with bright wooden beads. At rest the beads slide and click along the wires on the beat. Minute turn: the beads ride off the old wire as it re-bends smoothly into the new digit, then slide back on. Hour: every bead takes a ride through a loop-the-loop.

THEME: a Calder mobile and wire sculpture. Each numeral is drawn in black wire, hung from balanced arms with flat red, yellow, blue and black discs. At rest the mobile drifts and sways, the discs turn on the beat. Minute turn: the wire unbends and rebends into the new numeral while the arms rebalance. Hour: a draft spins the whole mobile while the time stays readable.

THEME: a candy shop taffy puller. Each numeral is a rope of glossy striped taffy. At rest the taffy stretches and sags on the beat, the stripes travel along it. Minute turn: the puller's hooks catch the old numeral, stretch and fold it, and lay it down as the new numeral. Hour: a big pull with the colour of the next batch folded in.

THEME: a fogged-up window on a rainy night, city lights behind. Each numeral is a finger-wiped stroke in the condensation, the bokeh of the street showing through it. At rest drops gather and run down the strokes, the lights behind pass and blink on the beat. Minute turn: the fog creeps back over the old numeral, then a finger writes the new one stroke by stroke. Hour: a passing tram floods the glass with light.

THEME: rhythmic gymnastics. Each numeral is drawn by a gymnast's long silk ribbon, in its own vivid colour. At rest waves travel down the ribbons and the gymnasts step and flick on the beat. Minute turn: the gymnast whirls the old shape into a spiral and snakes it into the new numeral. Hour: all four toss their ribbons high and catch them as the new time.

THEME: a soft-serve ice cream counter. Each numeral is a swirl of soft serve piped into the digit's shape, with sprinkles and a cone or cup, each a different flavour. At rest the swirl ridges travel, it drips and wobbles on the beat. Minute turn: the old numeral melts down into a puddle and the machine pipes the new one in one continuous ribbon. Hour: a sprinkle shower and a cherry on top.

THEME: a classroom geoboard. Each numeral is a coloured rubber band stretched over pegs on a plastic pegboard. At rest the bands twang and vibrate on the beat. Minute turn: the bands slip off pegs one by one and snap elastically onto new pegs to form the new numeral. Hour: a band flies off and pings around before every band re-stretches.
